author: BBC News
description:
Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 15 people including three children, according to officials.
 
The glide bombs hit residential buildings in the south-eastern city on Saturday morning. At least 16 others were injured in the attack, with more still missing and believed to be under the rubble.
 
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing "its thanks" for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump last night easing sanctions on Moscow to import Russian diesel.

title: Why have hundreds of 'cockroach' protesters been detained in Delhi? #Delhi #India #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
Protesters were heard slamming on bus windows following their detention during an anti-government demonstration called by The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi.
 
The CJP shared a video on social media showing its founder Abhijeet Dipke being detained with other leaders shortly after landing in the capital.
 
The movement started in May after India's Chief Justice likened some unemployed young people to "cockroaches".
 
Delhi police denied permission for the demonstration to take place, with tens of thousands of security personnel deployed and roads barricaded.
 
The CJP - and opposition parties - accuse Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party in the way the electoral rolls are being updated.
 
The Election Commission and the BJP have denied this.

author: BBC News
description:
AI can always be controlled, the president of encrypted messaging app Signal has told the BBC.
 
Meredith Whittaker said fears that AI could become conscious and take over were "not anchored in science and evidence", warning instead about the dangers of using the technology in military decision-making.
 
The former Google employee said AI could "supercharge mistakes" and reflected on her role in opposing the company's involvement in a US military drone surveillance project.
 
Speaking to the BBC Global Women, Whittaker also questioned who gets to shape the future of AI, criticised the concentration of power in Silicon Valley and explained why Signal would leave a country rather than compromise its users' privacy.

author: BBC News
description:
Tens of thousands of security personnel have been deployed and roads barricaded in Delhi to stop the latest Cockroach Janta Party demonstration.

The group says its leader, Abhijeet Dipke, is among hundreds who have been reportedly detained since Friday evening.

Dipke - who has said he is prepared to go to jail - started the movement in May almost as a joke in response to a remark by India's Chief Justice Surya Kant, who had likened jobless youngsters to "cockroaches".

author: BBC News
description:
Do you know your family medical history? For hundreds of thousands of care-experienced people, the answer isn’t always straightforward.

Missing medical and childhood information can affect access to healthcare, from identifying inherited conditions to getting an autism assessment.

In some cases, the consequences can be life-threatening, with people unaware of genetic conditions that could put them at serious risk.

BBC journalist Sophia Watkins travelled across the UK to meet adopted and care-experienced people, hearing how gaps in their records have affected their lives and what they’ve done to find answers.
